I am working on a small web service that stores user uploads and serves them back through a signed URL. The service runs behind a load balancer, and every request is authenticated with a short-lived token that the gateway validates before forwarding. Last week we started seeing intermittent failures when large files are uploaded from mobile clients on slow networks. The client reports a timeout, but the server logs show that the upload finished and the object was written to storage.

Please review the upload handler and explain why the client might time out even though the write succeeds. I suspect the handler waits for a checksum to be computed after the body is fully read, and that this step takes longer than the idle timeout on the load balancer. If that is the case, I would like to stream the checksum while the body is being read instead of computing it afterwards.

Before you change anything, describe the approach you would take and list the risks. Keep the public API the same, because several internal tools depend on the current response format. Add a regression test that uploads a file large enough to reproduce the delay, and make sure the test does not depend on the network. When you are done, summarize what changed and how you verified it.
